blocks.text: Forsskål, p. 1, describes a falcon with yellow cere and feet, ash-grey above, rust-coloured below, the wings dusky above, the tail forked, banded with dusky brown, of the length of the body. He renders the Arabic name of this bird in Latin letters as Haddai; perhaps the man from whose mouth Forsskål took down this name pronounced our حِداة [ḥidāh], plural حِداء [ḥidāʾ], with that sound. In an observation Forsskål adds the following: "Is it Falco Milvus Linn.? But it is neither wholly rust-coloured, nor is the head whitish. Is it Falco forficatus? But below it is not whitish, but rust-coloured." Hence in the newest edition of the Linnaean System, vol. 1, part 1, p. 261, this falcon forms a distinct species under the heading Aegyptius.
Michaelis has set out conjectures on the guesses of the ancients about this word in den Fragen an eine Gesellschaft von Gelehrten, die nach Arabien reisen, p. 303 ff.
